item.title: New Mexico Department of Transportation Secretary Ricky Serna to resign on February 20
item.description: NEW MEXICO (KRQE) – The head of the New Mexico Department of Transportation is stepping aside. NMDOT Secretary Ricky Serna announced on Monday that he will resign from his role on February 20. He served in that role for the past three and a half years. item.title: Quantum computing company chooses Albuquerque for U.S. expansion
item.description: ALBUQUERQUE, N.M. (KRQE) – Boston-based QuEra Computing, a company at the cutting edge of quantum tech, announced it is expanding to Albuquerque. The company has international locations; this will be its second U.S. headquarters. QuEra’s Chief Commercial Officer Yuval Boger said the company plans to make New Mexico a long-term home. item.title: Renovations underway on Alumni Pond at New Mexico State University
item.description: LAS CRUCES, N.M. (KRQE) – Renovations are now underway on the Alumni Pond at New Mexico State University. The university closed the pond back in 2023 after it lost much of its water in a short period of time. Restoration began last month and is expected to continue until late May. item.description: ALBUQUERQUE, N.M. item.title: More evidence gathered in rape cold case against Albuquerque man
item.description: ALBUQUERQUE, N.M. (KRQE) – The case against an Albuquerque man accused of raping two women more than a decade ago is growing. Carlos Parra-Cordova, 31, was arrested in 2023 after DNA from the two victims linked him to the crimes. item.title: Man gets life sentence for 2024 Albuquerque murder
item.description: ALBUQUERQUE, N.M. (KRQE) – An Albuquerque man was sentenced Monday for a 2024 murder in southeast Albuquerque. James Gonzales was sentenced to life in prison plus 24 years for shooting and killing 75-year-old Harry Velarde during a robbery.
